title: Resource-regret mapper: token-econ + latency sensitivity for roadmap scoring
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Problem: Current RICE-styled scoring at Redwood favors feature-level value proxies but under-weights token economics and latency regimes that materially change serving cost and customer experience. The Resource-regret mapper (RRM) is a pragmatic scoring overlay that combines traditional RICE factors with regret-adjusted resource impact for inference platforms.

Goal: Produce a repeatable rubric and tooling that: (1) quantifies expected token and compute delta per initiative, (2) maps latency-sensitive user cohorts to value multipliers, and (3) produces a single score used in roadmap tradeoffs and OKR alignment. Framework must be transparent to PM/Eng/Finance and produce per-initiative sensitivity curves.

Scope: Prototype scoring model + spreadsheet + dashboard inputs for top 30 backlog initiatives. Deliverables: scoring rubric doc, canonical CSV export, interactive notebook (Python) to run scenario sweeps, and a short playbook for quarterly roadmap debates.

Key components:
- Base RICE inputs: Reach, Impact, Confidence, Effort (kept for comparability).
- Token-econ delta: estimate of incremental tokens per user/week and mapped to cost/kg using current unit rates (hosted vs dedicated vs private).
- Latency sensitivity multiplier: cohort mapping (e.g., synchronous UI, background jobs, batch inference) with configurable penalties for latency > SLO.
- Regret factor: expected revenue or churn impact if capacity shortage leads to fallback/timeout. This converts severe availability/latency outcomes into an economic penalty.
- Capacity constraint overlay: flags initiatives that require dedicated capacity or On-Prem changes and escalate rollout effort.

Metrics/Success criteria:
- Framework adopted by PM review for Q2 roadmap decisions for at least 80% of mid-to-high complexity initiatives.
- Spreadsheet can be used to simulate token cost sensitivity (+/- 30%) and produce stable ordering for top 10 initiatives.
- Two example trade decisions (one where RRM reverses vanilla RICE ordering) documented and reviewed by Finance/Eng.

Risks & tradeoffs:
- Model requires reasonably accurate token-per-call estimates; we will use conservative ranges and surface uncertainty explicitly.
- Adds complexity to roadmap conversation — will provide simplified score + \"why it moved\" bullet for stakeholders.

Stakeholders: PM (Aisha K.), Eng (Liam C., Priya Rao), Finance (Marco Silva), Product Ops (Sara Nguyen), Observability lead (Diego Ortiz).

Next steps (week 1-3):
1) Kickoff workshop with Eng + Finance to align unit costs and latency penalties.
2) Build scoring spreadsheet and sample-run for 30 backlog items.
3) Iterate rubric with Design for concise visualization in roadmap deck.
4) Present pilot to GTM and Exec for feedback.

Artifacts:
- Draft rubric: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1rrm-example-rubric
- Working spreadsheet (canonical): https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1rrm-spreadsheet
